free_tier.stated: On 2026-10-23 the international free-trial documentation describes product trials as per-product resource quotas and solution trials as points: 'Points are deducted from the actual cloud-resource bills generated by the trial resources, at 1 point : USD 1.' The initial claim is 50 points, with 5 points per additional solution up to 10 solutions, valid for one year, and any single solution trial is capped at 168 hours. A separate promotion offers USD 200 on approval of a business use case.

egress.terms: inbound traffic is free and only outbound traffic is charged, by bandwidth or by traffic, at a region-dependent unit price (reference example USD 0.123 per GB in China (Hangzhou)); with CDT enabled on pay-by-traffic the free quota is 220 GB of Internet transfer a month (20 GB mainland regions, 200 GB regions outside the Chinese mainland); the CDT tiered overage price is not stated on the pages read
egress.free_allowance: 220 GB per month with CDT enabled (200 GB for regions outside the Chinese mainland, 20 GB for mainland regions)

interface_detail: the Alibaba Cloud CLI is documented; the ECS OpenAPI also has SDKs for common programming languages
tooling: the provider documents its own command-line tool, Alibaba Cloud CLI, per https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/cli/what-is-alibaba-cloud-cli: "Alibaba Cloud CLI is an open-source, cross-platform command-line tool that lets you do everything the Alibaba Cloud console does"
chaining: The money-denominated lane is now points at 1 point to USD 1, capped at an initial 50 points with one year of validity, so it buys a small trial rather than a season of compute. The earlier 200 GB a month of non-mainland egress is the term that would survive a quiet account if it still exists.

limits.value: 50 initial points at 1 point to USD 1, plus 5 points per additional solution up to 10 solutions, valid for one year, with any single solution trial capped at 168 hours

limits_note: the product trials are per-product resource quotas and the solution trials are points; the help page states no blanket signup credit
binding_note: the 168-hour per-solution cap stops any single long run first, and the 50-point initial claim plus the one-year validity bound the whole lane

identity_cost.detail: card at signup; a USD 1.00 pre-authorisation verifies the card; debit accepted if enabled for international payments; prepaid, gift, virtual and UnionPay-only cards refused because they cannot pass pre-authorisation; PayPal also supported; a verified phone number, and one identity may hold one account

notes: Two offers sit behind one brand and they are not the same door. The international lane takes a Visa or Mastercard and needs no national document, which is why this record is trial-only rather than fails-identity; the mainland lane at CNY 300 needs Chinese identity verification and is the one a user cannot open. The vendor's own community post says USD 90. The free trial page at alibabacloud.com/free is login-gated and served no content to any reader route, so the per-product list could not be read directly. Corrected on 2026-10-23: the earlier USD 90 over 3 months came from a localised page that the international help documentation no longer states. The money-denominated lane is now points at 1 point to USD 1 plus a USD 200 application. It is published: USD 1.00, on the payment FAQ. The refusal of prepaid, gift and virtual cards is confirmed there too, which is why prepaid counts as refused for this vendor.
